chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ali ibn Asbat from Ya'qub ibn Salim from Abi al-Hasan al-Abdi from Jabir al-Ju'fi from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites Yasin once in his lifetime, Allah writes for him virtues for every creature in the world and every creature in the Hereafter and in the heavens, and for every one of them two thousand good deeds, and erases from him a like number [of sins], and poverty does not afflict him, nor debt, nor ruin, nor fatigue, nor insanity, nor leprosy, nor whisperings [of doubt], nor a disease that harms him.

And Allah lightens for him the pangs of death and its terrors, and He takes charge of the departure of his soul, and he is among those for whom Allah guarantees abundant livelihood in his life, relief at his meeting [with Allah], and satisfaction with the reward in his Hereafter.
And Allah, the Exalted, says to all His angels, those in the heavens and those on the earth: 'I am pleased with so-and-so, so seek forgiveness for him.'

key_terms.سَکَرَاتِ الْمَوْتِ: The pangs or throes of death
key_terms.یَس: Surah Yasin, the 36th chapter of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting Surah Yasin once in a lifetime according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights Surah Yasin’s status as the 'heart of the Quran,' linking its recitation to comprehensive divine mercy. The text emphasizes both worldly protection from afflictions like poverty and illness, and spiritual ease during death, culminating in a unique divine declaration where Allah commands all angels to seek forgiveness for the reciter.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from Muhammad b. al-Hassan b. Abi al-Khattab from Ali b. Asbat from Ya’qub b. Salim from Abi al-Hassan al-’Abdi from Jabir al-Ju’fi from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said:

For one who recites Yasin once in his lifetime Allah writes for him virtues million times more than the number of Allah’s creatures that are in this world and would be in the heavens on the Day of Judgment, and the same number of his sins would be forgiven and that man would not be afflicted with poverty and sorrow: he would be safe from death by being buried under debris, misfortune, insanity and doubts and from every such illness that might give him pain, and Allah would make the pangs of death and its fear easy and light; and at the time of departure of the soul, Allah would be his Helper while for one whose helper is Allah there is generous livelihood in this world while in the next there would be happiness and pleasure before Allah and also a great reward.
When he meets his Lord in the Hereafter,
Allah would say to all the angels that exist in skies and the earth that I am happy and satisfied with such and such a man, so O angels, all of you seek forgiveness for this man.
